newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cosmonaut heart trouble delays Mir repairs.
newsitem.headline: Cosmonaut heart trouble delays Mir repairs.

text.p: Vital repairs to the crippled Mir space station may not take place for about ten more days because of minor heart trouble developed by the Russian commander, mission doctor Igor Goncharov said on Tuesday.

Doctors would recommend a course of treatment for commander Vasily Tsibliyev that would last "at best" ten days. If the Russians decided to replace Tsibliyev with NASA astronaut Michael Foale, the American would need a similar period to train for the risky and complex repair job, Goncharov told reporters.
A NASA official said earlier that Russian mission controllers had asked that Foale be prepared to do the repairs in Tsibliyev's place.
"If it is necessary we can do this," Philip Engelauf told reporters at Mission Control in Korolyov outside Moscow. British-born Foale had been fully trained for the mission.
Tsibliyev complained of cardiovascular problems on Monday. The repair works had been scheduled for Friday or Saturday.

During a radio link-up, Russian ground staff were heard by journalists telling Tsibliyev to do what he could to pass his experience of space walks to Foale, but also to tell the American he should not feel under pressure to accept the job.
